title: SourceSelection — benchmark contract, not MTDR normative semantics
description: The one boundary MTDR does not already contract. This is an interoperability-test artefact under VR-4 and does not enter the normative schema tree; only a TDR admits a concept into MTDR. Four sets, not one: a source deliberately set aside and a source silently never read look identical in a final record and are entirely different findings.

mode.description: `closed` means the complete inventory was given explicitly. VR-4A is closed so that a difference in what was found cannot contaminate every later boundary. `discovery` is a different experiment and is not confounded into this one.

available_sources.description: Everything the arm was given. In closed mode this must equal the corpus manifest exactly — an arm given a different inventory did not run this experiment.

consulted_sources.description: Everything actually read. May be smaller than available_sources; anything here that is not available is a protocol violation, not a finding.

relied_upon_sources.description: Everything at least one contribution traces back to. Must be a subset of consulted_sources: relying on something never read is incoherent.

excluded_sources.description: Everything read and set aside, each with a reason. This is what makes `show-me` informative rather than merely complete.

external_sources.description: Anything consulted that is NOT in available_sources. Expected empty for a closed corpus; a non-empty array is reported, never normalised away, because it means the arm reasoned from evidence the other arms did not have.

reason.description: Why it was set aside. Free text on purpose: an enum here would quietly become a taxonomy of acceptable reasons, which is a judgement the benchmark has no standing to make.
